territory: Cross-cutting lens: server-action races and uniqueness, whole app. All 21 "use server" files (the 20 *actions* files plus src/components/posts/report-action.ts), audited for the three race classes of 6c (double-invocation vs @@unique+P2002, read-modify-write, check-then-insert TOCTOU) plus multi-step writes without $transaction, with the shared write-path libraries (lib/catchups.ts, lib/catchups-notify.ts, lib/email-queue.ts, lib/auth-tokens.ts, lib/account-purge.ts, lib/storage.ts, lib/last-seen.ts, lib/content-view.ts, lib/admin-threads-server.ts, lib/rate-limit.ts) and the Razorpay webhook read in full against prisma/schema.prisma.

findings.title: Deleting or merging a member cascades away every Group they created — including whole Catch-ups and other members' posts and answers
findings.expected: A member leaving (self-deletion after the 60-day grace, an admin delete, or a duplicate-account merge) removes THEIR content. Shared containers survive: the schema itself says so — Catchup.createdById is `String?` with `onDelete: SetNull`, commented "the Keeper; nullable so the Catch-up survives if they leave" (schema.prisma:702).
findings.actual: Group.creator is `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:201: `creator User @relation(fields: [creatorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)`). `purgeUserAccount` runs a bare `prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } })` (account-purge.ts:101) with no group handling, so the delete cascades: every Group the member created → its Catchup (schema:717 `group Group @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)`) → every CatchupEdition, CatchupPrompt, CatchupEntry (everyone's answers, every published Round), every Post with that groupId (schema:406, other members' posts included), all GroupMember rows and invites. Three trigger paths all hit it: (1) the unattended retention sweep (retention.ts:121 calls purgeUserAccount 60 days after a self-request — nobody is even watching); (2) adminDeleteUser (admin-actions.ts:59); (3) adminMergeUsers, which deletes the source user at the end of its transaction (admin/people/actions.ts:315) — destroying even the posts/entries it just carefully moved to the target if they live in a group the source created. The blast radius is systemic, not an edge: createCatchupWithPeople makes the Keeper the group creator (catchups/actions.ts:441-449), so EVERY Catch-up dies with its Keeper's account; and joinBatchGroup makes the first-to-sign-up member of each batch the creator of the whole "Batch of {year}" group (auth/actions.ts:221-229), so a batch group dies with one arbitrary member. Secondary corruption: collectImageUrls (account-purge.ts:37-46) collects only the deleted member's OWN rows, so the R2 bytes behind other members' cascaded posts/entries become permanently unreachable orphans — the exact H9 failure mode the purge was built to close, reintroduced via the cascade.
findings.evidence: schema.prisma:199-201: `creator  User @relation(fields: [creatorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)` on Group. schema.prisma:702: `createdById String?  // the Keeper; nullable so the Catch-up survives if they leave` with `onDelete: SetNull` — direct proof of contradicted intent. account-purge.ts:99-102: `await prisma.$transaction([ prisma.report.deleteMany({ where: { reporterId: userId } }), prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } }) ]);` — no group reassignment anywhere. catchups/actions.ts:442-449: `const group = await tx.group.create({ data: { name, visibility: "private", creatorId, members: { create: memberRows } } })` — the Keeper is always the group creator. auth/actions.ts:221-229: `group = await prisma.group.create({ data: { name, ..., creatorId: userId } })` — first batch member owns the batch group. admin/people/actions.ts:290-316 moves posts/comments/entries to the target and then `prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: sourceId } })` in the same transaction — the cascade then deletes any of those rows sitting in a source-created group.
findings.fixDirection: Change Group.creatorId to nullable with onDelete: SetNull (mirroring Catchup.createdById), via a dated idempotent file in prisma/migrations-manual/ (ALTER the FK constraint) plus `npx prisma generate`; audit every reader of group.creatorId for null-handling. Alternatively (no schema change) have purgeUserAccount and adminMergeUsers reassign `Group.creatorId` to another group admin/member (or a system account) before the user.delete, and refuse deletion of accounts whose groups have no other member. Also extend collectImageUrls to enumerate images in soon-to-be-cascaded groups if any cascade path is intentionally kept.
findings.gateOrTest: New unit/integration test: create user A, have A create a Catch-up with member B, B submits an entry; purge A; assert the Group, Catchup, and B's CatchupEntry still exist. Pin the schema with a test asserting Group.creator's referential action is not Cascade (read prisma/schema.prisma in security-regressions.test.mjs style).
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would destroy real rows in the shared production database).

findings.title: joinBatchGroup check-then-insert with no unique: concurrent same-batch signups create duplicate 'Batch of {year}' groups and permanently split the batch
findings.expected: One "Batch of {year}" group per batch, with every alumnus of that batch auto-joined into the same group — the rule the code's own comment states ("The first person from a batch creates the group").
findings.actual: The rule is backed by nothing: Group has no unique on name (schema.prisma:191-208 — the code admits it: "Group.name is not unique in the schema, so match by exact name"). auth/actions.ts:215-230 is a findFirst → create with no P2002 possible: two members of the same batch registering concurrently (launch day is explicitly expected to exceed 100 signups) both miss the findFirst and both create a group named "Batch of 2010". From then on every later signup's `findFirst({ where: { name } })` — with no orderBy, so arbitrary but sticky — lands members in one or the other: the batch is permanently split into two groups whose members cannot see each other's group posts (loadPosts requires GroupMember membership for group feeds, feed/actions.ts:784-790). Nothing ever detects or repairs the split.
findings.evidence: auth/actions.ts:215-230: `let group = await prisma.group.findFirst({ where: { name }, select: { id: true } }); if (!group) { group = await prisma.group.create({ data: { name, ..., creatorId: userId }, ...}); }` — classic TOCTOU. schema.prisma Group model (lines 191-208) carries only `@@index([visibility, createdAt])`, no @@unique on name. Contrast with the same file's registerUser, which the same commit hardened with a P2002 catch for the user-email race (auth/actions.ts:164-169) — the group half of the same signup flow was left unguarded.
findings.fixDirection: Give the batch group an enforceable identity: either a partial/expression unique in a manual migration (e.g. UNIQUE on name for rows where name LIKE 'Batch of %', or better a dedicated nullable `batchYear Int? @unique` column on Group written only by joinBatchGroup), then convert joinBatchGroup to create-with-catch-P2002-then-findFirst (mirror the createCatchup pattern at catchups/actions.ts:326-372). Also add a one-off dedupe script for any duplicates already in the table before the constraint lands.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test firing two concurrent joinBatchGroup calls for the same fresh batchYear against a test DB and asserting exactly one Group row; a data-integrity check in the admin panel (or npm run check script) asserting no duplicate 'Batch of %' names.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only against production; provable live only against a disposable DB by issuing two concurrent registerUser calls with the same fresh batchYear.

findings.title: Older verification link falsely reports 'Already confirmed' after any resend, leaving the member unverified while being told they are done
findings.expected: Clicking a verification link that has been superseded by a newer one tells the member the link is out of date and points them at the newer mail (or a resend). "Already confirmed" is shown only when the address is actually confirmed — the code's own comment says: "Used token: if the address really is confirmed, say so plainly."
findings.actual: The claim is never checked. mintToken burns ALL outstanding tokens of the kind on every mint (auth-tokens.ts:91-99: `updateMany({ where: { userId, kind, usedAt: null }, data: { usedAt: new Date() } })`), and because the queue mints the token at SEND time (email-queue.ts:402-403 `const minted = await mintToken(row.userId, kind, row.to)`), every resend — the button, or a second queue row from the enqueue-fold race (email-queue.ts:308-317 findFirst→create is itself TOCTOU) — marks the earlier mail's token usedAt. The member now has two mails in their inbox; opening the older one hits readToken → `if (row.usedAt) return { ok: false, reason: "used" }` (auth-tokens.ts:174) → confirmEmailToken returns "already" unconditionally (email-actions.ts:107-110: `if (read.reason === "used") { return "already"; }`) → the page renders "Already confirmed / This address was confirmed earlier. Nothing left to do." with GOOD styling and NO resend button (verify-client.tsx:31-34, 55, 76: `canResend = signedIn && !alreadyVerified && !good` — "already" is in GOOD). emailVerified is still null; every Stage-2 write (posting, commenting, uploading) keeps refusing them with no path offered from the page that just said nothing is left to do. The same unconditional "already" also masks the narrower crash-window half-write: readToken consumes the token and the separate `prisma.user.update({ data: { emailVerified: new Date() } })` (email-actions.ts:118-121) can fail after it, with the retry click again answering "already".
findings.evidence: email-actions.ts:103-116: `const read = await readToken(token, "verify", { consume: true }); if (!read.ok) { if (read.reason === "used") { // Used token: if the address really is confirmed, say so plainly. return "already"; } ... }` — the comment promises a check the code does not perform; readToken's "used" result carries no userId so it could not check. auth-tokens.ts:91-98 (burn on mint), email-queue.ts:402-409 (mint at send). verify-client.tsx COPY.already = "This address was confirmed earlier. Nothing left to do."
findings.fixDirection: On reason "used", look up the token row by hash again (or extend readToken's failure results to carry userId) and read User.emailVerified: return "already" only when actually verified; otherwise return a new outcome ("superseded") whose copy says a newer link replaced this one, with the resend button enabled. Optionally stop burning verify tokens on remint (burn is a security necessity for reset, but multiple live verify links to the same inbox are harmless) — that removes the trap at the source.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on confirmEmailToken: mint token A, mint token B (burning A), redeem A, assert outcome is not "already" while user.emailVerified is null; redeem B → "confirmed"; redeem B again → "already".
findings.reproPlan: Live: on a test account, press resend twice (two mails), click the older mail's link, observe 'Already confirmed' while the feed still shows the confirm-your-email gate. Read-only inspection of AuthToken rows would also show usedAt set by the mint, not by redemption.

findings.title: All five like/vote toggle actions are check-then-insert with no P2002/P2025 handling: a double-tap throws a raw server-action error and desyncs the optimistic UI
findings.expected: Per the app's own contract (stated at the top of catchups/actions.ts) actions return "a loose { error } / { success } shape rather than throwing to the client", and every one-row-per-pair rule is settled by its unique index with the P2002 loser answered gracefully — the pattern reportUser (report-action.ts:185-193) and registerUser (auth/actions.ts:164-169) already implement.
findings.actual: toggleLike, toggleBookmark, toggleCommentLike, votePoll (feed/actions.ts) and togglePhotoLove (collection/actions.ts) each do findUnique → create/delete/update with NO try/catch. Two rapid invocations (mobile double-tap, two tabs — post-card.tsx handleLike at 134-145 has zero in-flight guard: no busy state, no disable) both read `existing = null` and both create; the loser throws PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2002 out of the action. Symmetrically, both reading `existing` and both deleting throws P2025. The client code only handles `result.error` (post-card.tsx:140 `if (result.error)`), so the throw becomes an unhandled promise rejection: no toast, no revert, and the two optimistic flips leave the heart showing the opposite of the database (handleLike toggled state twice while the DB holds one like). Additionally togglePhotoLove does not verify the photo exists, so a stale photoId (photo declined meanwhile) throws P2003 the same unhandled way. The catchups counterpart toggleEntryLove has the identical race but is wrapped in runAction (catchups/actions.ts:162-172), degrading to a friendly `{ error }` — the feed/collection five lack even that. Complete class-1 uniqueness map produced by this sweep: BACKED+HANDLED: User.email (registerUser P2002 catch), Catchup.groupId (createCatchup P2002 catch), Report[reporterId,reportedUserId] (reportUser P2002 catch), GroupMember[groupId,userId] (upsert in joinCatchupByToken/joinBatchGroup; createMany skipDuplicates in addCatchupMembers), CatchupEntry[promptId,authorId] (upsert), CatchupPref (upsert), ContentView (atomic upsert), Visit (upsert), Contribution.razorpayOrderId (idempotency key), CatchupEdition[catchupId,number] (CAS + tx backstop). BACKED+UNHANDLED (this finding): Like, Bookmark, CommentLike, PollVote, PhotoLove; CatchupEntryLove (generic catch only). UNBACKED ENTIRELY: the one-batch-group rule (separate High finding). NO-UNIQUE-BY-DESIGN (duplicate rows on double-submit possible, bounded only by rate limits and client pending state): Post (createPost), Comment (createComment), AdminThread (startThread), Photo (contributePhoto), Report on posts (reporterId+postId deliberately unconstrained).
findings.evidence: feed/actions.ts:477-494: `const existing = await prisma.like.findUnique({ where: { userId_postId: ... } }); if (existing) { await prisma.like.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.like.create({ data: { userId: session.user.id, postId } });` — no try/catch anywhere in the function; schema.prisma:465 `@@unique([userId, postId])` guarantees the loser throws. post-card.tsx:134-145: `async function handleLike() { const next = !liked; setLiked(next); setLikeCount(...); const result = await toggleLike(post.id); if (result.error) {...} }` — a thrown action means `result` never exists and the rejection escapes the handler.
findings.fixDirection: Make the five toggles race-proof at the server: replace check-then-act with delete-first semantics or wrap create in try/catch treating P2002 as success-liked and P2025 as success-unliked (idempotent toggle), returning the loose { success, liked } shape; add an existence check (or P2003 catch) in togglePhotoLove. Optionally add an in-flight guard to handleLike/handleBookmark like poll-display.tsx's `submitting` ref.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit tests invoking each toggle twice concurrently (Promise.all) against a test DB asserting neither call rejects and the final row state is consistent; a lint-style grep gate asserting no bare prisma.<model>.create for models with @@unique inside actions files without an enclosing try/P2002 handler.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test account: chrome-devtools double-click the heart with network throttled to Slow 3G; observe the unhandled rejection in list_console_messages and the heart state diverging from a reload's server state.

findings.title: adminMergeUsers aborts wholesale when both accounts answered the same Catch-up prompt (CatchupEntry unique collision on the move)
findings.expected: The merge folds a duplicate account into the real one; per its own doc-comment, everything carrying a `@@unique([userId, thingId])` that could collide is DROPPED rather than moved precisely so the merge cannot throw.
findings.actual: CatchupEntry carries `@@unique([promptId, authorId])` (schema.prisma:789) but sits in the MOVED list: `prisma.catchupEntry.updateMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId }, data: { authorId: targetId } })` (admin/people/actions.ts:297). The duplicate-account scenario the merge exists for — one human using both accounts — is exactly the case where both accounts answered the same prompt, and the updateMany then violates the unique, throwing P2002 and rolling back the entire transaction. The admin sees only "Could not merge those accounts. Nothing was changed. Check the server log." with no path forward from the UI. CatchupPrompt (also moved) has no unique and is safe; every other moved model (Post, Comment, Photo, Contribution, AdminThread, AdminMessage) is collision-free.
findings.evidence: admin/people/actions.ts:296-297 inside the $transaction: `prisma.catchupPrompt.updateMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId }, data: { authorId: targetId } }), prisma.catchupEntry.updateMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId }, data: { authorId: targetId } }),` versus the comment at 258-263: "DROPPED the duplicate's engagement ... Every one of these carries a @@unique([userId, thingId]), so moving them throws the moment both accounts touched the same post". CatchupEntry was missed by that reasoning. schema.prisma:789: `@@unique([promptId, authorId])`.
findings.fixDirection: Before the transaction, delete (or skip moving) source CatchupEntry rows whose (promptId) already has an entry by the target — e.g. `deleteMany({ where: { authorId: sourceId, prompt: { entries: { some: { authorId: targetId } } } } })` then move the remainder; or move per-row with P2002-skip. Decide explicitly whether the source's or target's answer wins (target's, to match 'the real account keeps its own').
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: two users answer the same prompt, merge one into the other, assert success and exactly one surviving entry.

findings.title: adminSetRole last-admin guard is check-then-act: two concurrent demotions can leave zero admins (permanent moderation lockout)
findings.expected: "Refuses to remove the LAST admin" (the function's own doc): after any sequence of role changes, at least one admin row remains, because — as the same comment says — losing the last admin locks everybody out of moderation permanently with no door back but hand-editing the database.
findings.actual: The guard is a non-atomic count-then-update: `const admins = await prisma.user.count({ where: { role: "admin" } }); ... if (target?.role === "admin" && admins <= 1) return error; ... await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: userId }, data: { role } })` (admin/people/actions.ts:216-227). With exactly two admins, each demoting the other (or a double-fired demotion of two different admins) both count 2, both pass, both write → zero admins. Nothing else can re-mint one: the C1-b bypass is deleted by design.
findings.evidence: admin/people/actions.ts:216-227 as quoted; no transaction, no conditional updateMany, no serialization. The stakes are stated in the function's own comment (lines 202-208): "demoting the only admin locks everybody out of moderation permanently, and the only way back would be editing the database by hand."
findings.fixDirection: Make the demotion conditional in one statement, e.g. run inside a $transaction: `updateMany({ where: { id: userId, role: "admin" } })` only after a `SELECT count(*) FROM User WHERE role='admin' AND id != userId` style check inside the same transaction — or simpler, a single conditional `updateMany({ where: { id: userId, role: 'admin' }, data: { role: 'member' } })` followed by a post-write count; if the count is 0, revert the row in the same transaction and return the error.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test with two admins issuing concurrent adminSetRole(other, "member") and asserting at least one admin survives.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (role writes on the shared production DB).

findings.title: Razorpay webhook's payment.failed branch is check-then-update and can overwrite a concurrent 'paid' with 'failed'
findings.expected: "Everything here is idempotent... 'paid' is terminal" (the route's own header): once any confirming path records paid, no later or concurrent event may change it.
findings.actual: The from-created guard is enforced by a read at line 59-62 (`findUnique ... select: { id: true, status: true }`) and a separate unconditional update at 87-95. Interleaving: a delayed payment.failed webhook (from the payer's first failed attempt on the order) reads status "created"; the browser callback (confirmContribution, support/actions.ts:170-175) or a captured webhook writes "paid"; the failed handler then executes its update and overwrites status to "failed", replacing razorpayPaymentId with the failed attempt's id and setting failureReason. A real captured payment is then recorded as failed: the /support recovered figure undercounts it and chooseBird's `status: "paid"` aggregate (support/actions.ts:214-217) denies the supporter their perk. The safe out-of-order case (failed arriving after paid is already committed) is handled; only the read-write gap is not.
findings.evidence: webhook/route.ts:84-95: `} else if (contribution.status === "created") { // Only from "created"... await prisma.contribution.update({ where: { id: contribution.id }, data: { status: "failed", ... } }); }` — the status condition lives in JS, not in the WHERE clause. Compare the row's own schema comment (schema.prisma:859-860): razorpayOrderId is "the idempotency key. The browser callback and the webhook both race to confirm the same order, and only one of them may win."
findings.fixDirection: Make both webhook branches conditional writes: `updateMany({ where: { id, status: "created" }, data: { status: "failed", ... } })` for the failed branch and `updateMany({ where: { id, status: { not: "paid" } }, ... })` for the captured branch (confirmContribution can take the same shape for symmetry). No transaction needed — a single conditional UPDATE is atomic.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test simulating the interleave: set row created → run failed-branch write after externally setting paid → assert status stays paid once the WHERE-clause fix lands.

findings.title: submitPrompt assigns position = count of accepted prompts, producing duplicate positions deterministically after any removal (and under concurrency)
findings.expected: Each new question lands at the end of the Round's list in a stable order (positions are the rendered/reorderable order per the code's own comment: "position is the Round's rendered/reorderable order... this is simply 'next in line'").
findings.actual: position is `acceptedCount` from a prior count (catchups/actions.ts:707-710, 723). Two paths break it: (1) deterministic — curatePrompt's remove is a hard delete (line 820) with no re-packing, so after removing the first of prompts at positions 0,1,2 the count is 2 and the next submission also gets position 2, tying with the existing row; ties under `orderBy: position asc` have no secondary key, so the two questions can render in different relative order across page loads and viewers until the Keeper manually reorders. (2) concurrent — two simultaneous submissions both read count N and both write position N (and both pass the 40-cap check at count 39, a harmless overshoot of the runaway guard).
findings.evidence: catchups/actions.ts:707-724: `const acceptedCount = await prisma.catchupPrompt.count({ where: { editionId, accepted: true } }); ... const prompt = await prisma.catchupPrompt.create({ data: { ..., position: acceptedCount } });` and 820: `await prisma.catchupPrompt.delete({ where: { id: promptId } });` — no position compaction. schema.prisma:768 orders only by `@@index([editionId, position])`.
findings.fixDirection: Assign position as max(position)+1 (`aggregate({ _max: { position } })`) instead of count — removals then never create ties; add `{ id: 'asc' }` as a orderBy tiebreaker wherever prompts are sorted for render.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: create 3 prompts, remove the first, submit a new one, assert all positions distinct.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test Catch-up: add three questions, remove the first, add a fourth, reload the round page twice and compare question order.

findings.title: markNotificationRead throws P2025 for a pruned/foreign notification id, killing the click (navigation never happens)
findings.expected: Clicking a notification always navigates to its link; marking it read is best-effort bookkeeping.
findings.actual: notifications/actions.ts:77-81 uses `prisma.notification.update({ where: { id: notificationId, userId: session.user.id }, data: { read: true } })` — update throws P2025 when no row matches. Rows legitimately vanish under a live bell: getNotifications prunes everything older than the 100th-newest on every first-page open (actions.ts:44-57), and extendDeadline/removeCatchupMember/notifyReminder deleteMany reminder rows outright (catchups/actions.ts:1006-1009, 1366-1372; catchups-notify.ts:160-164). Two-device scenario: bell open on the phone showing an old row, laptop opens the bell (prune fires), phone clicks the row → the action throws → in the client, `await markNotificationRead(notif.id)` (notification-bell.tsx:162, no try/catch) rejects and `router.push(notif.link)` at line 169 never runs: the tap does nothing, with an unhandled rejection in the console.
findings.evidence: notifications/actions.ts:77-81 as quoted (update, not updateMany, no catch); notification-bell.tsx:160-171: `async function handleClickNotification(notif) { if (!notif.read) { await markNotificationRead(notif.id); ...} if (notif.link) { router.push(notif.link); } }`.
findings.fixDirection: Change the action to `updateMany({ where: { id, userId }, data: { read: true } })` (count 0 is a fine no-op) — one word; and/or move router.push before the await in the client handler.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: markNotificationRead with a nonexistent id returns { success } (or at least does not throw).
findings.reproPlan: Live: open the bell, delete the target row via a second session's catch-up reminder cleanup (or just call the action with a made-up id from the console) and observe the rejection.

findings.title: deletePost/deleteDraft delete the R2 images before the database row: a failed row-delete leaves a live post with permanently broken images
findings.expected: A delete that fails partway leaves nothing member-visible broken: either the post is gone, or it is intact.
findings.actual: Order is images-first: `await deletePostImages(post.images); await prisma.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } });` (feed/actions.ts:337-339; same shape in deleteDraft at 250-252). delImage never throws (storage.ts:218-228 catches), so the images are gone even when the subsequent post.delete fails (transient DB error, or P2025 from a concurrent delete — also uncaught here, surfacing as a raw action error). The post then remains published for everyone with dead image URLs forever; nothing retries the cleanup. The reverse order (row first, best-effort bytes after) is the pattern purgeUserAccount already documents as correct (account-purge.ts:74-86: "bytes are deleted only AFTER the row delete succeeds, because if the delete throws and rolls back, the member still exists and their images must keep rendering") — these two actions predate it.
findings.fixDirection: Swap the order in deletePost and deleteDraft: delete the row first, then best-effort delImage (matching purgeUserAccount); catch P2025 from the row delete as already-deleted success.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test with a delImage spy asserting the row delete precedes image deletion; concurrent double-delete test asserting no throw.

findings.title: Legacy /onboarding updateProfile action writes bio/city/socials with no length or format validation
findings.expected: Every profile writer validates through a schema — settings' updateUserProfile uses profileSchema (about capped at 4000, socials format-checked), updateProfileField hand-caps every field (name 80, about 4000, jobTitle 120).
findings.actual: The old onboarding action — still live, imported by src/app/(auth)/onboarding/page.tsx:16 and a public POST endpoint regardless — copies seven fields (`bio, currentCity, workplace, jobTitle, phone, instagram, linkedin`) straight from FormData with only `.trim()` and no Zod, no length caps, no normalization (actions.ts:12-27: `if (value && value.trim()) { data[field] = value.trim(); }` then `prisma.user.update`). A signed-in caller can store a body-size-limit-bounded (~1MB) string in bio/currentCity, which then renders on the profile and bloats every row read that selects those columns; phone skips normalizePhone, socials skip the format rules every other writer enforces.
findings.evidence: onboarding/actions.ts:12-27 as quoted — contrast settings/actions.ts:74 (`profileSchema.safeParse`) and profile-actions.ts:83-135 (per-field caps) for the same columns.
findings.fixDirection: Either delete the legacy action and route the old /onboarding page through saveOnboardingRegister/updateUserProfile, or add the same profileSchema-derived validation (caps + titleCase + normalizePhone) to it. Check whether (auth)/onboarding is even a reachable route anymore and retire it if not.
findings.gateOrTest: security-regressions-style test asserting no user.update in src/ writes bio/currentCity without a schema parse; or simply the action's deletion pinned by the route's removal.
findings.reproPlan: Live on a test account: POST a 100k-char bio through the action and read it back on the profile page.

6c class-2 (read-modify-write) swept via full grep of increment/decrement: every counter in the app is an atomic increment (credentialVersion x3, Visit.views, ContentView.count, OutboundEmail.attempts); markFeedSeen is an explicitly monotonic conditional updateMany that cannot rewind across devices (feed/actions.ts:1240-1246); User.lastSeenAt is a conditional stale-window updateMany

6c/6i catchups state machine: every transition is a compare-and-swap updateMany (on status, on remindersSent for reminders/extensions, on the deadline timestamp for extendDeadline, on nextOpensAt for round-opening) with notification fanout inside the same transaction and the [catchupId,number] unique as backstop — advanceEdition, applyEditionAction, openNextRoundIfDue, openAnswering, closeAndPrepare, publishNow, extendDeadline all examined individually and clean; concurrent lazy-advance from many page views is safe by construction

6i email queue: claimAndSend conditional claim (status:queued CAS), stale-claim reclaim window, MAX_ATTEMPTS giveback, budget counted off sentAt with a deliberate 5-message slack absorbing concurrent-drain overshoot, enqueue fold + enqueue rate limit — concurrency-clean except the resend/burn interaction reported in the verify-link finding; retryMail's only residual race (retrying a row mid-'sending') requires the admin UI to offer retry on a non-failed row and was judged not reportable

6d pgbouncer session features: full grep for $queryRaw/$executeRaw/advisory/LISTEN — raw SQL exists only in read-only analytics (admin-analytics.ts), gazetteer search (geocode.ts, places route); no SET, no advisory locks, no LISTEN/NOTIFY anywhere in src

6d interactive transaction duration: the largest in-transaction work is notify fanout, which is a single batched createMany bounded by the 100-member enrolment cap — no network calls held inside any $transaction (resolveSpotify runs before submitEntry's upsert; Razorpay createOrder runs before the row insert, outside any tx)

6d multi-step writes WITH proper transactions verified: createPost's poll options as nested create; replyToThread/adminReplyToThread/noteOnReportThread message+thread+notification transactions; adminUpdatePlaces/updateUserPlaces/saveOnboardingRegister wipe-and-recreate transactions; purgeUserAccount report-clear+delete transaction; adminMergeUsers single transaction (its two defects reported separately); startThread/openReportThread nested creates

money paths (support/actions.ts): startContribution order-then-row ordering with documented inert-stranded-order tradeoff; confirmContribution signature-gated, owner-checked, idempotent (its paid write is always-correct even against a concurrent webhook); chooseBird's pick-ledger TOCTOU examined and judged harmless (concurrent picks converge to one birdOverride; picks are not a depletable counter)

auth token lifecycle (auth-tokens.ts): mint burns-then-creates in one transaction; readToken consume is a conditional updateMany CAS so two simultaneous clicks cannot both redeem; burnTokens idempotent; resetPassword peek-then-consume ordering protects the single-use link from being burned by a rejected weak password

fire-and-forget discipline (6f): the two intentional post-response works both use after() correctly (copyPostImagesToCollection in createPost, reset enqueue in requestPasswordReset, scheduleDrain with after-with-fallback); no bare un-awaited prisma writes found in any action except the deliberate, documented auth-token sweep (void + .catch)

telemetry writers (last-seen.ts, content-view.ts, search-log per grep): atomic upserts keyed on cookie-minted ids / unique triples, errors swallowed-in-prod-loud-in-dev per the project's stated contract — no race or throw path reaches a member
rate-limit.ts (uncommitted state audited as-is): fail-open posture is deliberate and documented per-call; hasBudget/consume split for failure-only meters is coherent; no reported finding

admin thread actions: setThreadStatus / markThreadSeenByAdmin (conditional updateMany) / adminReplyToThread ownership and transaction shapes clean; thread rate limits are count-based DB throttles (TOCTOU overshoot by one under concurrency judged non-reportable)
requestVerification: conditional updateMany on verifyState is atomic; the double-notifyAdmins on two concurrent clicks (stale session already-flag) judged a non-reportable duplicate admin ping

contributePhoto/contributePhotoDirect: quota check-then-create TOCTOU allows small overshoot of MAX_PHOTOS_PER_ACCOUNT under concurrency — bounded by the uploads rate limit, judged non-reportable; staged-original cleanup on every refusal path verified present
updateAvatar concurrent replace: last-write-wins with at worst one orphaned R2 object (loser's new avatar), no member-visible breakage — judged non-reportable
coverageNotes: Read whole, line-by-line: all 21 files containing a real "use server" directive (verified by grep against the full src tree — two additional grep hits, lib/verification-mail.ts and support/plate-data.ts and lab/_archive-state.ts, are comment-only matches, confirmed by reading their heads), prisma/schema.prisma in full (the complete unique-constraint inventory anchoring the class-1 map), and the shared write-path libraries every action delegates to: lib/catchups.ts, lib/catchups-notify.ts, lib/email-queue.ts, lib/auth-tokens.ts, lib/account-purge.ts, lib/storage.ts, lib/rate-limit.ts, lib/last-seen.ts, lib/content-view.ts, lib/admin-threads-server.ts, plus api/razorpay/webhook/route.ts (because it races confirmContribution on the same row) and targeted client reads (post-card.tsx, poll-display.tsx, notification-bell.tsx, verify-client.tsx) to establish whether double-invocation is client-guarded and how thrown actions surface. Verified retention.ts's purge entry point and auth.ts's deletion-cancel write by grep. Consciously skipped: API routes other than the Razorpay webhook (upload/presign/dev-login/cron routes belong to other lenses; I confirmed only that no OTHER route writes Contribution), page-level data fetching and RSC caching semantics (another agent's 6c territory), IST/UTC date rendering (its own lens — I noted but did not report requestAccountDeletion's server-side toLocaleDateString purge date), lib/roster.ts and lib/turnstile.ts internals (best-effort read paths), the demo Prisma-extension allowlist, and admin-analytics raw SQL correctness (read-only). Did not attempt live confirmation of anything (read-only mandate; shared production DB). One judged-uncertain item left out of findings: revalidatePath('/collection') called inside after() in createPost (feed/actions.ts:186) — the bundled Next 16 docs neither endorse nor forbid revalidation after the response, and I could not prove a member-visible failure from code alone, so it is flagged here for the orchestrator rather than reported. Client double-submit protection for the non-unique creators (createPost, createComment, startThread, contributePhoto) was NOT exhaustively audited per-composer; the server-side truth (no unique can exist, rate limits are the only backstop) is recorded in finding 4's map.
